messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] feature request for log(x-y); given log(x) and log(y), i.e. a log_diff_exp(xl, yl)
parts:
[from stan-users]


Given that we know x > y, we can just do this:

   log(exp(x) - exp(y))

   = log(exp(x) * (exp(x)/exp(x) - exp(y)/exp(x)))

   = log(exp(x)) + log(1 - exp(y)/exp(x))

   = x + log(1 - exp(y - x))

   = x + log1m(exp(y-x))

Because x > y, 0 <= exp(y-x) <= 1.

This article here talks about log(1-exp(-|a|) (and related functions), which would also be good to have since this function log_diff_exp the way you suggest could use it and is also a useful thing by itself (I needed this function log1m_exp a couple of times, in fact).

I've just created the function log1m_exp and pushed to my fork, with unit tests included. If you wish I can pull request it after some more tests and also take care of:

log_diff_exp(x,y) = x + log1m(exp(y-x)) = x + log1m_exp(y - x)    (when x>y)


Just to point out the conclusion of the article I mentioned: basically, log1m_exp(.) than is better than log1m(exp(.)) whenever we have 0>y-x>-log(2), otherwise, it uses log1m:
      if(a>=0) BOOST_THROW_EXCEPTION(std::domain_error ("x cannot be greater or equal to zero")); //this is what log1p does
      else if(a > -0.693147) return log(-boost::math::expm1(a)); //0.693147 is approximatelly equal to log(2)
      else return log1m(exp(a));


And here's the result of a model created to test it (comparing result given by R using the function in the article):

do more of these kinds of operations more stably. It's
going to make me look back into how some of our other
functions are implemented.

I checked out your fork and that code looks great.
It's even what I would've called the function.

The only other things to do are:

a) test the gradient vs. auto-diff of log(1 - exp(x))
b) add a model that uses them in all possible configurations of
data and parameter inputs and assignments
c) add forward-mode auto-dif

We can catch up on forward-mode if you don't want to do
that. It's for Riemann Manifold HMC and Hessian-based
optimization, but it's not used anywhere yet.

I'm about to roll out a new template pattern for implementing
special functions like this that'll automatically vectorize
them and implement them for forward-mode and reverse-mode
auto-diff variables.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan-users] feature request for log(x-y); given log(x) and log(y), i.e. a log_diff_exp(xl, yl)
parts:
My problem is how to test what you said:
The only other things to do are:

a) test the gradient vs. auto-diff of log(1 - exp(x))

For example, running a simple model:

parameters { real test; } model { lp__ <- lp__ + log1p_exp(test); test~normal(0,1); }
yields:
./model --test_grad
  param idx           value           model     finite diff           error
         0       -0.811444         2.11903         2.11903     1.78911e-10

I am under the impression that:
>> "model" is the value of gradient calculated via reverse automatic differentiation
>> "finite diff" is: "divided differences", that is, f'(x) ≈ ( f(x+h) - f(x) )/h, for some small h
>> "error" is: model - finite diff

So "test the gradient vs. auto-diff" would mean check that the "error" is not big, am I right?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan-users] feature request for log(x-y); given log(x) and log(y), i.e. a log_diff_exp(xl, yl)
parts:
Exactly, but you can should do it with a call to the
lib, not to a compiled model. We have some libs for
it floating around in Stan, so you shouldn't need to
reimplement finite differences from scratch.

It's usually better to do this:

df/dx =approx= f(x+epsilon/2) - f(x - epsilon/2) / epsilon

- Bob
